Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Practical review mining mechanics for extracting identity markers (e.g., "I am a...") and mapping social media subcultures to identify unserved sub-niches. modules: [AVT] topics: [research method, review mining, segmentation, market sophistication] tier: 4 scope_hint: mixed

Topics. research method / identifying avatars via simple Google Forms, customer interviews, and social media trend analysis. review mining / searching competitor and generic marketplace reviews for identity-based keywords. market sophistication / how increasing sophistication forces broad markets to fracture into specialized sub-avatars. segmentation / "nesting doll" sub-segmentation (e.g., broad athletic apparel -> gym-goers -> specific gym subcultures).

Look for. Specific review mining mechanics: scanning generic marketplace or competitor reviews for phrases like "I am a [job title]" or "As a [role]" (e.g., "As a nurse on my feet all day...") to uncover hidden buyer segments. Survey techniques: using free tools to ask existing buyers to describe their specific role, unique situation, and how the product helps them. Subculture mapping: tracking how a mass market splits into hyper-specific demographic or psychographic avatars (e.g., general fitness fracturing into distinct segments for female-only, alternative/misfits, or entrepreneur-focused lifters). The strategy of monitoring emerging recreational trends (e.g., cornhole) to be the first dedicated brand for a newly forming avatar.

Skip. Persona templates with generic demographics. Any instruction on copying competitor Facebook ads, writing primary text, or building landing pages, as these belong in downstream application modules and will poison the discovery focus of this module.

Scope mix. The method of finding avatars via reviews and surveys is baseline. The degree of sub-segmentation (niching down into a fraction of a market) is growth, gated by the level of market sophistication.
